subject: Azura Therapeutics — one-time onboarding discount request
messages:
From: Laura Martinez <laura@azuratherapeutics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: one-time onboarding discount for Azura Therapeutics

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile. We're under a tight procurement window and have budget constraints in Q3. Azura is prepared to sign a 12-month committed usage agreement (~$1.8M ARR run-rate) but needs a stronger upfront concession to move forward this week.

Specifically, procurement is asking for a one-time onboarding discount/credit that effectively reduces year-one spend by ~35% (applied as an onboarding credit against the first two invoices). If Redwood can confirm approval within 48 hours we can get a PO over to you and finalize legal.

I attached our PO template for your review (Azura_PO_template.pdf). Can you let me know if this is something you can escalate for an exception?

Best,
Laura Martinez
Director, Strategic Procurement
Azura Therapeutics

[attachment: Azura_PO_template.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Martinez <laura@azuratherapeutics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: one-time onboarding discount for Azura Therapeutics

Hi Laura — thanks for the note and the PO template. Great to hear the demo resonated.

We can escalate this for an exception, but I want to be transparent about typical guardrails: a 35% effective reduction on a $1.8M run-rate is outside standard commercial authority and will need VP/CFO approval. That said, there are a few ways we can structure a concession that preserves economics while addressing Azura's timing:

- limited-duration onboarding credit (defined dollar amount, amortized over first 2 invoices)
- accelerated prepay discount in exchange for earlier payment
- contract term/commitment floors to protect unit economics

I'm routing to Kimberly and Jordan internally to pull financials and draft an exceptions memo. Please hold off on sending the PO until we come back — aiming to respond within the 48-hour window you requested.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: AZT-1098: request for one-time onboarding concession — need VP/CFO sign-off

Kimberly / Jordan —

Looping you in on an urgent exception request from Azura Therapeutics (see thread below). Key facts:
- Estimated ARR run-rate: ~$1.8M (first-year committed consumption).
- Customer ask: one-time onboarding credit equal to ~35% of year-one bill (applied to first two invoices).
- Timing: procurement needs confirmation within 48 hours to finish internal approvals.

Why this matters: Azura is a high-value strategic biotech with potentially broader workflow adoption across their R&D stack. Approving a structured exception could accelerate expansion, but the requested credit level materially impacts margin and sets a precedent.

Requested actions:
1) Jordan — can you run a quick finance impact calc (ARR, gross margin delta, payback) and confirm whether we can offset with a term or payment condition? Please flag any accounting or revenue recognition concerns.
2) Kimberly — can you draft a succinct VP/CFO memo that outlines the ask, recommended structure, and decision request (approval / revise / deny)? I can surface to VP as soon as it's ready.

Attachments: azura_pricing_request_summary.pdf (summary I've prepared from the call)

I can take point on negotiations/DocuSign once we have an approved structure. Time is tight on this one — appreciate quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Marissa

[attachment: azura_pricing_request_summary.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: AZT-1098: request for one-time onboarding concession — draft recommendation

Thanks Marissa — reviewed the summary. My suggested compromise to preserve precedent and economics:

Recommendation (commercial):
- Approve an onboarding credit equal to 25% of the first-year committed ARR, implemented as a $450,000 credit applied across the first two invoices.
- Require a 12-month committed minimum and either (A) 60-day upfront payment on invoice 1 with a 3% prepay discount OR (B) standard payment terms plus an additional 6-month minimum extension (total 18 months).
- Include a one-time non-transferable clause and explicit language that credit is not precedent for other accounts.

Rationale: the credit is reduced from the ask (35% -> 25%) and paired with payment/term protections to recover margin over time. This should make the economic hit manageable while giving Azura the upfront concession they requested.

I've drafted a memo for VP/CFO sign-off (attached: azura_exception_memo_draft.docx) — it includes the ask, the proposed structure, financial impact, and recommended approval language. Jordan, please confirm the numbers and add any accounting/recognition caveats.

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

[attachment: azura_exception_memo_draft.docx]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: AZT-1098: request for one-time onboarding concession — finance calc and next steps

Kimberly / Marissa — quick finance check attached (finance_impact_calc.xlsx). High-level:
- Approving the 25% credit as a $450k onboarding credit reduces year-one recognized revenue by ~$350k after amortization (assuming the credit is applied across invoices and recognized over the period).
- Gross margin impact is material in Q3 but payback under the 12-month commitment + prepay option looks acceptable (IRR improves with upfront payment).
- Accounting caveats: if we treat the credit as contra-revenue, we need to ensure the contract references to avoid channel misclassification; revenue recognition will follow standard ASC rules — no unusual blockers flagged.

I support the recommended structure conditionally — final approval must come from VP/CFO (Kimberly's memo is fine to present). Please route the attached memo + calc to VP/CFO for signature. If we get signoff today I agree we can accept the PO and proceed to DocuSign.

Jordan Blake
Director, Finance — Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference

[attachment: finance_impact_calc.xlsx]
